calibration_source: Eurostat (namq_10_gdp, namq_10_pe, namq_10_a10_e, demo_pjanbroad, lfsi_emp_a), OECD LFS, ECB

x_comments.alpha_K: Capital share set to 0.33 for cross-country comparability with Germany and Poland, both of which use 0.33 in the Ramsey layer. PWT labsh for Spain implies alpha nearer 0.38-0.40, but holding alpha_K fixed across countries keeps the Ramsey trends comparable and avoids a BGP K/Y that diverges from the other two models for a purely measurement-driven reason.
x_comments.delta_annual: 5% annual depreciation for total-economy capital, matching Germany rather than Poland's 6%. Spain's capital stock is unusually structures-heavy after the 1998-2007 construction boom, and structures depreciate slowly; the growth model matches total GFCF (Eurostat P51G) including those structures, so the lower rate is the right one.
x_comments.beta_annual: Discount factor: 0.96 annual, same as Germany and Poland. It pins the terminal modified-golden-rule BGP real rate jointly with sigma and tfp_growth_annual; the resulting r* is written to output/documentation_data/ramsey/ramsey_summary_Spain.json (structural.r_star_annual) by calibrate_growth_model rather than quoted here, because it is derived and would go stale.
x_comments.sigma: Inverse IES (CRRA coefficient). sigma=1.5 is mid-range consensus (1=log, 2=high risk aversion), same as Germany and Poland.
x_comments.tfp_growth_annual: 0.4% annual labour-augmenting TFP growth, DERIVED FROM THIS SAMPLE rather than assumed. Over 2000q1-2025q1 the Spanish levels data give GDP per hour growth of 0.60% p.a.; on a BGP where K grows with Y, g_A = g_(Y/L) * (1 - alpha_K) = 0.60% * 0.67 = 0.40%. This is close to Germany's 0.5% and consistent with the well-documented stagnation of Spanish TFP over this period. It is deliberately NOT set to zero: measured Spanish TFP growth is near zero over 2000-2013 and recovers after, and a zero or negative trend would give a degenerate BGP. Revisit if the sample is extended.
x_comments.phi: Inverse Frisch elasticity on extensive margin. PROVISIONAL: set to 1.3 (the German value, calibrated there from a SimPaths wage-shift response surface). No Spanish SimPaths experiments exist yet, so this carries no Spain-specific information and should be re-estimated from dedicated Spanish SimPaths runs when available. Same status as Poland's 1.35.
x_comments.labor_supply: Default Ramsey labor-supply mode. calibrate_growth_model.m copies this template into the bundle folder input/ES/MacroModel/ and writes the calibrated runtime fields there.

base_year_values.WAP_comment: Working-age population (15-64), thousands. Source: Eurostat demo_pjanbroad (A.NR.Y15-64.T.ES), Spain 2000 = 27,787,317 persons. Must match build_population_projection.m age range.
base_year_values.x_comment: calibrate_growth_model.m writes calibrated base-year levels and derived fields into input/ES/MacroModel/growth_params_Spain.json.

inflation_target.x_comment: ECB 2% target - Spain is a euro founder member, so the same target as Germany applies for the whole 2000q1 sample. Differs from Poland's 2.5% NBP target. pi_star entered as annual percent.

labor_trends.nawru_source: PLACEHOLDER: HP trend (lambda=160000) of the in-sample ILO unemployment rate, written by calibrate_growth_model.m. Intended source: AMECO.
labor_trends.demographic_L_source: PLACEHOLDER: HP trend (lambda=160000) of the in-sample labour force, written by calibrate_growth_model.m; no projection tail. Intended source: Eurostat population projections + INE labor force participation.
labor_trends.x_comment: nawru_file is read for diagnostics only. demographic_L_file has no post-sample tail, so ramsey_trend.m extends N at its trailing 20-quarter trend growth rate, untapered, until build_population_projection.m supplies a projection. Hours: log-linear trend fitted to observed.

solver.x_comment: Stacked-time Newton (LBJ) perfect-foresight solver with terminal K/Y closure. 400 terminal quarters (~100 years) as for Germany; Poland needs 600 only because its terminal_growth block has to converge a catch-up TFP path, which Spain does not have. Newton convergence requires ||F||_inf <= 1.0e-10 within 200 iterations.
